Authored only from trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-R revision); the 005-Q acceptance suite was read for format only (schema, case keys, mention-group notation and the forbidden-pattern notation, whose generic polarity patterns are reused with the activity and hour words replaced). No code, run output or other suite was read. Focus, two-case evidence (spec 5, 005-R): positives where the answer must state both cases A05R-01, A05R-02, A05R-03, A05R-40, A05R-43, A05R-61, A05R-62, A05R-63, A05R-67; sub-code exception negatives where only the first case is required A05R-59, A05R-70, A05R-71; cross-language two-case passages where the check does not apply A05R-44, A05R-45. Ambiguities recorded: (1) Spec 6 (005-R revision) lets the system notice supply missing mentions, incl. a left-out case quoted from the evidence; the two-case mention groups are still written so a correct model answer meets them on its own. (2) Whether a bracketed source title before the first case counts toward that case's words was decided after review: spec 5 (005-R) leaves a leading [title] out of the word comparison. The word rule is lexical: a paraphrased one-case answer can escape it and a paraphrased both-case answer can get an unneeded retry and notice; no expected value depends on it. (3) For cross-language passages the spec only says the check is skipped; no other rule requires the second case, so those cases require only the general (main) case and do not forbid the other. (4) 'Names only a different sub-code' is read as: the second case's subject is a different sub-code of the asked family, even when the sentence also carries condition words (as in the spec's own example '다만 T-5-3 …'); the other side is then neither required nor forbidden.
